Action Plan:
1. Urgent electronic referral to local TIA (Transient Ischemic Attack) / mini-stroke clinic for assessment within 1–2 days, including carotid Doppler ultrasound and possible brain imaging.
2. Provide patient with TIA clinic and PALS telephone numbers; advise calling this afternoon or tomorrow morning to confirm appointment.
3. Safety-net advice: If neurological symptoms recur and are prolonged, attend Emergency Department immediately; otherwise contact GP for further review.
4. Advise patient he may be contacted by phone by the stroke team; ensure availability.
5. Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.

Subjective:
• 32-year-old male presents with episodic neurological symptoms for 1.5–2 months.
• Symptoms: fatigue → right-hand pins & needles → right arm weakness, transient right-leg weakness/abnormal gait; episodes initially weekly/monthly, now several times daily, each lasting a few days, then resolving.  
• Associated only during episodes: difficulty holding coffee cup, mild throat sensation, transient nausea. No speech or visual disturbance, no persistent dysphagia.
• No current symptoms at time of consult.
Past Medical History: none reported.  
Family History: father with carotid surgery for stroke prevention.  
Medications: Aspirin 75 mg once daily (dose/route/frequency as stated; self-initiated).  
Social: Non-smoker; lives with wife; employed as plastic-surgery doctor.  
Allergies: Penicillin.

Objective:
• Telehealth; video lost midway.  
• Patient asymptomatic during call; no physical examination performed or vitals recorded.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Episodic right-sided weakness/paraesthesia  
   - Assessment: Suspected Transient Ischemic Attack (TIA).  
   - Differential: migraine aura, focal seizure, demyelinating disease; less likely given presentation but to be excluded by specialist clinic.  
   - Investigations planned: Urgent TIA clinic work-up (carotid ultrasound, brain imaging, blood tests as per protocol).  
   - Treatment planned: None initiated in consult; await specialist assessment.  
   - Referrals: Same-day electronic referral to TIA clinic.

2. Self-initiated Aspirin use  
   - Assessment: Aspirin 75 mg OD without documented indication.  
   - Investigations planned: None ordered.  
   - Treatment planned: No change to medication documented during consult.  
   - Relevant referrals: Nil.

Quality checks:
● Missing but expected: neurological examination, cardiovascular exam, blood pressure, full medication/allergy reconciliation, current vitals.  
● Internal conflicts: None identified.  
● Transcript quality: Moderate; intermittent audio/video loss but clinically relevant information obtained.
